rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only models. This tests the simplest RNA-only configuration (pca_n2000 encoder, singleprofile) to understand baseline performance before exploring more complex multimodal or image-only setups. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoding and profile settings while keeping other factors minimal, aligning with the principle of reducing uncertainty about key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that using a singleprofile RNA-only model with PCA achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) with the same RNA encoder, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploration of multiprofile benefits while keeping RNA encoder consistent, providing critical insight into whether profile aggregation improves performance without complicating other factors.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002: 0.590664 accuracy) outperform singleprofile ones. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation) improves accuracy. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising multiprofile direction without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that using multiprofile with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005, 0.65 accuracy) outperforms other RNA-only settings. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising scvi_n200 encoder while maintaining other successful parameters, balancing exploitation of the current lead with targeted exploration.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether switching to the scgpt RNA encoder (a more advanced model) with the same transformer aggregation and multiprofile setting could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining consistency in other parameters, providing critical insight into whether this choice is a key factor in performance gains.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.653). This experiment tests a logical extension by combining this RNA encoder with an image encoder (resnet50) using concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation of the current best RNA configuration with exploration of multimodal potential, which could yield higher accuracy if image data adds value.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.65297). This experiment tests combining these strong components with multimodal settings and weighted fusion, which could enhance performance by leveraging both RNA and image data effectively. It directly addresses whether multimodal approaches with optimized components can surpass unimodal baselines.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) while keeping other components the same, isolating the impact of the image encoder. This is the best use of the remaining budget to explore a critical design choice with high potential for improvement.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (used in config_039) with scgpt, while keeping other components identical, could further improve performance. This comparison isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong prior evidence for the other components to focus on uncertainty about the RNA encoder.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion to compare RNA encoder impact while maintaining the effective aggregation method. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice, which has shown mixed results, and uses the proven aggregation method from config_039.
